title: People Power for Florida: Volunteer Orientation

We’re having conversations with everyday Floridians about the issues that matter most and **empowering them to register to vote and get involved.**

This is how we fight back—**and we need you with us.**

**📢: Join us for a virtual volunteer orientation call on the second Monday of the month.** Learn how you can take action right now in your own community, connect with other passionate volunteers, and strategize with People Power for Florida organizers to **reach and mobilize new voters in your community.**

#### This training will cover:

- ✅ How to register voters 
- ✅ How to collect ballot initiative petitions 
- ✅ Strategies to expand our outreach in your community 
- ✅ How to engage with your policymakers
- ✅ How to get involved with People Power

The stakes have never been higher. **Now is the time to organize, mobilize, and build power—together.**


RSVP today, and let’s get to work.

title: Franklin Township, NJ: Rally to Stop The NESE Pipeline
description:
The NESE pipeline is BACK. **Trump wants to fast-track this dangerous polluting project here in Central Jersey — and we need your help to stop it again!**

On Thursday evening, the Franklin Township Council will consider a resolution opposing NESE once again. Join us to rally at 6 p.m. in front of the Franklin Municipal Complex (at the gazebo) ahead of the meeting to show strong opposition to this zombie project.

Municipal resolutions send a powerful message to the Governor and other decision-makers and are an effective way to push for change at the local level. **Join us to speak out against this un-NESE-sary pipeline!**


### About NESE:

The Northeast Supply Enhancement (NESE) proposal calls for construction of a gas-powered gas compressor station in Franklin Township, as well as 3.5 miles of connecting pipeline through Old Bridge and 23 miles of new pipeline under the Raritan Bay / New York Harbor.

NESE would pollute our water, increase flooding, destroy critical wetlands and habitats, and would cut through the already-polluted and sensitive Raritan Bay and New York Bay. Pipelines leak enormous amounts of methane, a stronger greenhouse gas than CO2, which directly contributes to climate change.

The proposed compressor station in Franklin would release air- and water-polluting toxins. The gases emitted by a compressor station can increase the risk of asthma as well as cardiovascular, neurological, developmental, and respiratory diseases.

This project is not in the public interest for New Jersey residents. Our communities in New Jersey will receive the direct impacts of pipeline leakage and compressor station pollution, while none of the gas is even for New Jersey.

**We defeated NESE last year, and we can do it again. Join us as we get organized and rally against zombie NESE!**

title: Working Class Workshops
description:
Hello future candidates! Ready to take the next step to get ready for your campaign? Welcome to Working Class Workshops, your week-long training and workshop sessions that will keep your momentum moving toward victory. These sessions are built to be equal parts learning and application, as we discuss campaign fundamentals such as fundraising, narrative, social media, and the kinds of campaigns needed to win governing power for the working class of all races. Excited to keep learning? Sign up for our virtual sessions and let’s get to work!  

The schedule of trainings are as follows [each session will be held virtually at 6:30PM - 8:30PM CDT]: 

Monday, June 23rd: Building Independent Political Power
This session will be exploring WFP’s theory regarding how to build governing power for the working class of all races and what we believe about elections, candidates and the role of a political party. 

Tuesday, June 24th: Communications: Message and Narrative
This session will be teaching and workshopping with participants the best skills and practices for authentically connecting our individual stories to a larger narrative that fuels the messages that a campaign will be communicating to their voters.  

Wednesday, June 25th: Past Candidates and Current Electeds Panel
This session will be centered around the experiences, guidance and wisdom that our panel of former candidates and current elected leaders will share with participants. 

Thursday, June 26th: Finding and Funding Our Why
This session will be grounded in fundraising principles and tactics - while using concepts learned in Communications: Message and Narrative to construct commonly used tools such as elevator pitches, life lists, and making a strong fundraising ask.

Friday, June 27th: Social Media Workshop
This session will be teaching participants how to strategically use social media as an effective campaign and messaging tool, including mythbreaking common misconceptions about social media platforms, tips for candidates and campaign staff, and relatable examples of campaigns using social media to their highest potential.

title: NO DICTATORS - Oslo, Norway

location.venue: Frogner Park - Meet at Lincoln monument

description:
Please join Democrats Abroad Norway members and others in Oslo on Saturday, June 14 in a global day of defiance and solidarity against authoritarianism.

We’ll be gathering at the Abraham Lincoln monument in Frogner Park from noon to 2pm (12:00-14:00) LOCAL TIME (GMT+2) for silent as well as vocal protest. We’re calling it No Dictators Day – our counter-birthday party for Donald Trump, in conjunction with hundreds of similar events in the U.S. and around the world. Bring your friends and family, and above all bring your enthusiasm, your voice (since there will be singing) and your matpakke (since it will be lunchtime).

We’ll celebrate the eloquence and achievements of perhaps our greatest president in comparison to the failures and absurdities of a self-congratulatory would-be monarch who fawns over his own birthday with an unnecessary and ridiculously expensive military parade. Americans revere our 16th president as much for the lofty, hopeful rhetoric of what he wrote and said, as for his signal accomplishments: the preservation of the Union and his more prosaic yet powerful proclamation that slaves shall henceforth be free.

But Lincoln could never have predicted our 45th and 47th president’s lust for power and his acolytes in Congress’ kowtowing to his every whim.

It’s up to us to listen to Abe on Flag Day, to appeal to the better angels of our nature and to help stop the wickedness and folly.

Note that because Norway DOES have a king, we are calling our event "No Dictators." Please do not bring signs with "no kings" language out of respect to Norway. The image is set by No Kings and cannot be changed.

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

title: Hennepin County Attorney Community Relations Board Town Hall
description:
Join us in Minneapolis for our community event, What’s The Role of a County Attorney, Anyway?

We're partnering with the Minnesota Justice Research Center and the Legal Rights Center for a community event to educate our neighbors on the roles and responsibilities of the County Attorney’s Office on Thursday, June 26, 2025, from 6:00 PM to 8:00 PM at UROC 2001 Plymouth Ave, N, Minneapolis, MN 55411. Food and drinks on us! Will you attend?

Join us for an engaging evening of discussion with community leaders about the critical role of prosecutors in shaping our criminal legal system. Prosecutors hold immense power at every stage of the criminal process—from deciding who to charge and with what offense, to recommending sentences that impact individuals and families for years to come.

This event will spotlight the collaborative efforts of the Hennepin County Attorney Community Relations Board in addressing these issues. Through meaningful conversations, good food, and a welcoming atmosphere, we’ll explore what’s at stake for our communities and how we can drive meaningful change together.

Don’t miss this opportunity to deepen your understanding, connect with others, and renew your commitment to justice and equity in our community.
